executive_summary.one_paragraph: COVE User Service is a reactive Spring Boot microservice deployed on AWS EKS that provides JWT-based authentication, user registration with admin-approval workflows, and role-based access control for the COVE platform. Primary users include end-users registering for accounts (CUSTOMER role) and administrators managing user onboarding, account activation, and role assignments (ADMIN role). The system integrates with external OneView API for project performance data, uses AWS RDS MySQL for persistence, and sends email notifications via Gmail SMTP. The architecture follows a layered pattern with Spring WebFlux for reactive programming, stateless JWT authentication, and comprehensive audit logging for compliance.

key_characteristics.characteristic: Reactive microservice architecture with Spring WebFlux
JWT-based stateless authentication with access tokens (30 min) and refresh tokens (24 hours)
Admin-approval workflow for user onboarding with email notifications
Role-based access control (CUSTOMER and ADMIN roles)
Comprehensive audit logging for administrative actions
AWS EKS deployment with automated CI/CD via AWS CodeBuild

drivers.rationale: System handles sensitive user credentials, PII, and requires audit trails for administrative actions. JWT-based authentication with token revocation, BCrypt password hashing, and comprehensive action history logging are implemented.

Reactive programming with Spring WebFlux enables non-blocking I/O for high concurrency. Stateless JWT authentication allows horizontal scaling. AWS EKS deployment with 2 replicas and resource limits supports auto-scaling.

Prometheus metrics exposed via Spring Actuator for monitoring. Kubernetes health checks and readiness probes configured. Audit logging for administrative actions supports compliance and incident investigation.

System integrates with OneView API for performance data, Gmail SMTP for notifications, and Netflix Eureka for service discovery. Integration patterns include REST API calls, SMTP email delivery, and service registry updates.
Business requirement for admin approval of new user registrations before account activation. Onboarding workflow with pending_approval, approved, and reject states enforces this control.

integration_architecture.summary: System integrates with 7 external touchpoints: OneView API (outbound REST for performance data), AWS RDS MySQL (outbound JDBC for persistence), Gmail SMTP (outbound SMTP for email notifications), Netflix Eureka (bidirectional REST for service discovery), Prometheus (inbound HTTP scrape for metrics), AWS ECR (outbound Docker Registry API for image storage), and AWS EKS (bidirectional Kubernetes API for orchestration). Authentication patterns include custom token-based (OneView), basic auth (MySQL, Gmail), and unknown for infrastructure services. No explicit retry logic except OneView fallback to previous day's data; relies on library defaults.

data_architecture.summary: Data persistence uses AWS RDS MySQL 8.0.33 with four primary tables: users (user profiles and credentials), access_token (short-lived JWT tokens), refresh_token (long-lived JWT tokens), and action_history (audit log for admin actions). JPA entities define schema with auto-DDL generation. Relationships include one-to-many from users to tokens and logical association to action_history via email. No database migration tool detected; schema evolution relies on JPA auto-DDL.

persistence_and_flow_notes.note: User credentials stored with BCrypt hashed passwords; email field is unique index
JWT tokens stored in plain text (signed but not encrypted at rest) with expiration and revocation flags
Action history records all admin actions with timestamps and admin attribution for audit compliance
No caching layer detected; all data access goes directly to MySQL
Database connection does not explicitly configure SSL/TLS encryption

security_and_privacy_architecture.summary: Security model uses JWT-based stateless authentication with access tokens (30 min validity) and refresh tokens (24 hours validity). Passwords are BCrypt hashed before storage. Role-based access control enforces CUSTOMER and ADMIN roles with protected /api/v1/admin/** endpoints. Token revocation on logout and login. Audit logging for all admin actions. Critical security risks identified: hardcoded OneView API credentials in source code, plain text credentials in configuration files, missing SSL/TLS for database connection, no rate limiting on authentication endpoints, no account lockout mechanism, and no MFA implementation.

control_highlights.description: Stateless JWT tokens with signature validation, expiration checks, and database-backed revocation
BCrypt hashing for user passwords before storage
CUSTOMER and ADMIN roles with endpoint-level authorization enforcement
Comprehensive action history for all admin operations with timestamps and attribution
Assumed based on production deployment context; not explicitly verified in code

business_alignment.summary: Software architecture directly supports six primary business processes: User Registration (creates pending approval records), Admin Onboarding Approval (approves/rejects registrations with email notifications), User Login (validates credentials and generates tokens), Token Refresh (extends authenticated sessions), Admin Account Management (activates/deactivates accounts), and Admin Role Management (changes user roles). All admin actions are logged for audit compliance. The onboarding workflow enforces business requirement for admin review before account activation.
